study.question: Observed limitation: no unified exchange candidate has beaten baseline-din click AUC 0.65554408. The exchange Q1/W1 cell scored 0.64745824 versus Q0/W0 0.63229720, but its Q-by-W interaction was negative (-0.00644144), so both positive simple effects do not establish complementarity. The mass family improved its best cell to 0.65333041, still below DIN. The value-residual family scored 0.65146720 at R1/Q1 versus 0.64948071 at R0/Q1 and 0.65063769 at R1/Q0 versus 0.65054808 at R0/Q0: raw values helped within that family, but the family did not improve the best mass ancestor. These are single-seed validation observations, with no candidate slice or mechanism diagnostics requested. Does field/history feedback improve retrieval when both rounds retain DIN's full field-concatenated matching and unnormalized direct-value pooling, relative to an equally sized stacked interaction control?
study.hypothesis: The prior trajectories leave a joint scoring/representation mismatch plausible: mass scaling and a post-retrieval raw-value residual do not restore full-width item-field interactions in the scorer. This is a provisional explanation, not an established bottleneck. Construct a first DIN read, mix user/context fields, target fields and its full-width history summary in a small MLP, and send that state back into a second shared-parameter DIN read. Q adds a bounded query residual; W applies a bounded feature-wise gate to matching keys only. Both reads pool the original item/action values without normalization. Their average and both refinement vectors reach identical task heads. This permits field interaction and history selection to evolve together while preserving a direct native-value path. Q0/W0 provides the same learned feature interaction and repeated scorer calls but disables both feedback edges. The principal test is feedback versus this stacked control; the bundle comparison against DIN cannot by itself identify why earlier rank-32 architectures lost. Novelty relative to original unified methods remains unverified.

nearest_work.difference: Read archived primary arXiv:1706.06978v4, lines 216-298, including the local-activation sum and absence of softmax at lines 266-277. Inherit local item/target interactions and unnormalized direct-value pooling. Add a field/history interaction state and a second retrieval with independently controlled query/key feedback. The local four-task reference is an adaptation, not an exact original DIN reproduction.

Read pinned benchmark implementation at git:90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d, lines 105-283, source SHA256 22b11a32da1fdcc65790377e20dddaf6663961cf47c99cae66c452bbcffc81d0. It alternates query mixing, sequence refinement, cross-attention and fusion. This candidate uses one full-width field-concatenated query, shared DIN local scoring, original unprojected values, and strict pre-score/value masks. W modulates matching keys only; it neither applies a sequence FFN nor rewrites value content. This is a nearby information-flow reference, not a MixFormer reproduction or local efficacy claim.

Resolved and attempted to read the original-method reference; detailed text is unavailable in the authorized registry. Followed fallback unirank-benchmark-v2 section 2.3 and inspected its pinned implementation. Differences are established only against that benchmark implementation; original-paper priority and originality remain unresolved.

Only the archived author README is available, not the blocked publisher paper. It warns that its behavior data contains category, brand and behavior type without item IDs. Our fixed input contains prior advertisement IDs and real item fields; no DMR reproduction, missing-item substitution, or transfer claim is made.

study.proposed_difference: Replace the compressed exchange family with a native-matching refinement architecture, using baseline-din as empirical parent. Let p0=DIN(target, original_keys, original_values). Let h=GELU(Linear([context,target,p0])) with width 128, dq=tanh(Linear(h)), dk=tanh(Linear(h)), each with native key width. Read again using query target+0.5*dq if Q=1, otherwise target; matching keys keys*(1+0.5*dk) if W=1, otherwise original keys. Values always remain original. Task heads consume [context,target,(p0+p1)/2,dq,dk]. All four cells instantiate identical learned modules, use all of them in the heads, and execute both reads in the same order. Q/W only switch feedback edges. Erase padded keys/actions before scoring and mask final scores; empty histories yield exactly zero p0/p1. No target action, task mask, label or unavailable timestamp is used. Unlike temporal sequence encoders, this design remains permutation invariant over valid history events. Its tested mechanism is iterative history selection, not order modeling.
predictions: Working prediction: native_q1_w1 improves validation click AUC over native_q0_w0. Report all four cells and every task's AUC/Logloss; auxiliary mean AUC does not select models. Beating the smaller DIN reference is a separate performance question.

Query-feedback simple effects are A11-A01 and A10-A00; key-feedback effects are A11-A10 and A01-A00, where Aij denotes native_qi_wj click AUC. Positive effects would provide local controlled support for the corresponding feedback route, pending repetitions. A11-A10-A01+A00 tests complementarity, which is not established by either positive main effect.

A11 exceeding both single-route controls would favor retaining both routes. If only one route helps, retain the simpler supported direction rather than claiming a joint mechanism. If all four improve similarly over DIN, extra stacked interaction/capacity is the leading explanation.

If the host exposes authorized history slices, use the existing empty, 1-16, 17-64 and >64 bins, with sample/positive/negative counts. History-read effects should be absent for empty histories conditional on the same learned weights. Across trained cells, empty-history predictions can still differ because Q changes shared-scorer learning. Slice interpretations remain exploratory without paired repetitions.

All cells have identical parameter counts and sparse embedding dimensions. If C is context embedding width, K native item-key width, V value width and F=C+K+V, added parameters relative to the reference are 128*F+128+2*(128*K+K)+4*(2*K*128). Two large local scorer calls should cost more than one DIN call. No efficiency advantage or equal-compute superiority is predicted without measured allocation, memory and latency.
falsifiers: Nonpositive A11-A00 fails the joint-feedback benefit prediction for this implementation and frozen recipe. Nonpositive query or key simple effects reject that route's local benefit at the corresponding other-factor setting. Nonpositive factorial interaction fails the complementarity prediction even if individual routes help.

If the strongest native cell does not beat baseline-din, the new implementation has not improved the selection metric. A gain over earlier exchange families alone cannot establish full-width scoring as the cause because normalization, heads, representation and positional treatment also changed.

If gains are matched by Q0/W0, feedback is not the supported explanation. If point estimates disappear or reverse under paired seeds or available user-cluster uncertainty analysis, do not claim repeated mechanism support.

Nonfinite forward/backward values, incorrect [B,1] task probabilities, nonzero pooled values for all-empty history, or dependence on altered masked history/target action fail implementation integrity before scientific comparison. Such failures consume budget and do not refute the mechanism.
alternative_explanations: Extra MLP and head capacity, improved optimization in the frozen single pass, and random seed variation may explain gains versus DIN. Q0/W0 controls capacity, modules and repeated reads within this batch; the original DIN is not capacity matched.

Full-width local scoring, unnormalized signed weights, shared scorer parameters, absence of position input, mask handling and new heads change together relative to the exchange ancestors. This batch cannot separate those causes; a later matched scorer/normalization replacement would be needed.

Dice running statistics are updated twice per training forward in every native cell and can differ between refreshed and fixed reads. This is part of the implemented training dynamics; it is not a pure inference-time routing comparison. Original DIN updates once. Padding is erased before the scorer in all new cells; the original reference did not explicitly do this.

Q and W may be redundant reparameterizations of the nonlinear matching function rather than complementary information channels. The factorial estimates expose this possibility. Both refinement vectors reach the heads, so switches affect both second-read values and their gradient routes; forward-only causality is not isolated.
A bounded residual gain of 0.5 is an uncalibrated architecture choice, not a tuned optimum. Failure may reflect that choice or the one-epoch recipe, rather than all iterative retrieval structures.

The empty/short-history baseline slices are weaker than the long-history slice, but prevalence and cohort difficulty differ. This is not evidence of lost order information. The proposed architecture remains order invariant and does not test recency or long-history truncation.

The inherited official_offline delayed-feedback visibility and whole-window vocabularies/static snapshots limit production claims. Auxiliary category/brand-based labels are not advertisement-specific conversion attribution.
